topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20265 → #20257. See plan §13 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Scope

~7 files in `op-devstack/sysgo/` call `ethclient.Dial` / `ethclient.NewClient` directly. Most are for L1 contract deployment and faultproof dispute-game setup; but the files need a per-call audit:

- `op-devstack/sysgo/add_game_type.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/singlechain_build.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/l1_runtime.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/multichain_supernode_runtime.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/superroot.go`

L1 callers stay on `*ethclient.Client` — upstream-safe. Any L2 caller migrates to `op-service/sources.EthClient`.

topIssues.title: kona-node: support static peers
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
kona-node can only find peers through discv5, seeded by `--p2p.bootnodes`. It has no equivalent of op-node's `--p2p.static`: a comma-separated list of multiaddrs that op-node dials at startup, treats as trusted, and keeps connected (`op-node/flags/p2p_flags.go`).

This matters more once discovery is opt-in. The planned kona-node CLI turns discv5 off by default (`--p2p.discovery.enabled`), so without static peers a node with default settings connects to no one. Sequencers behind op-conductor commonly run without discovery and peer only with known nodes.

Static peers also keep a cluster connected when discovery cannot: on a local conductor devnet, the consensus clients split in two when the only bootnode came back on a new IP with an empty table.

Most of the pieces exist in `rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/`: `Driver::dial_multiaddr`, the connection gater's protected peers (exempt from the redial limits), and the admin connect-peer path in `rust/kona/crates/node/actors/src/network/`.

### Proposal
- Add `--p2p.static-peers <MULTIADDR,...>` (env `KONA_NODE_P2P_STATIC_PEERS`).
- Dial each static peer at startup as a protected peer.
- Redial a static peer whenever its connection closes.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A kona-node with discovery off and static peers connects to them at startup and reconnects after either side restarts.
- [ ] Static peers are never banned or dropped by the redial limits.
- [ ] A test covers the reconnect.

topIssues.title: op-devstack, op-acceptance-tests: read L2 blocks through the partitioned sources accessors
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20265 → #20257. See plan [§11](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md#L300). Follow the sources-client rules in #20265, with #23417 as the worked example.

## Problem

The op-devstack DSL and op-acceptance-tests read L2 blocks through `apis.EthClient`'s `InfoAndTxsBy*`. [That path](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-service/sources/eth_client.go#L375-L411) decodes every tx with go-ethereum. It works today only because the build resolves to op-geth. After the go.mod flip (#20266) it fails on the deposit (`0x7E`) and post-exec (`0x7D`) txs in every L2 block. It compiles fine, so the ratchet (#23407) cannot see it.

## Sites (L2 endpoints only; the L1 uses stay)

- **DSL:**
  - [`l2_el.go` `AssertTxNotInBlock`/`AssertTxInBlock`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-devstack/dsl/l2_el.go#L711-L740). These must still match deposit hashes. Combine `InfoAndUserTxs` with `InfoAndDeposits` (`optypes.DepositTx.Hash()`).
  - [`l2_network.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-devstack/dsl/l2_network.go#L159)
  - [`fjord_fees.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-devstack/dsl/fjord_fees.go#L152)
  - [`operator_fee.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-devstack/dsl/operator_fee.go#L140)
- **Acceptance tests:**
  - [`jovian/da_footprint.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-acceptance-tests/tests/jovian/da_footprint.go#L195). This test correlates txs with receipts by position, so filter receipts in lockstep by type.
  - [`jovian/bpo2/joviantest/cases.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-acceptance-tests/tests/jovian/bpo2/joviantest/cases.go#L257)
  - [`fjord/check_scripts_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-acceptance-tests/tests/fjord/check_scripts_test.go#L126)
  - [`fusaka/fusaka_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-acceptance-tests/tests/fusaka/fusaka_test.go#L66)
  - [`batcher/throttling/throttling_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher/throttling/throttling_test.go#L49). It reads `InfoAndTxsByLabel(Unsafe)`, and no by-label partitioned accessor exists. Add `InfoAndUserTxsByLabel` in this PR, or resolve the label to a hash first.

Re-derive the list with `git grep -nE 'InfoAndTxsBy(Hash|Number|Label)' -- op-devstack op-acceptance-tests` and classify each by endpoint.

## Notes

- No accessor returns post-exec (`0x7D`) txs (§11). On Lagoon+ presets, tests that count a block's txs need to account for that.
- `fjord_fees.go` and `operator_fee.go` also carry #23405's symbol swaps (op-geth cost functions, receipt fee fields). Do both in one PR, or sequence them.

## Acceptance criteria

No DSL or acceptance-test code calls `InfoAndTxsBy*` on an L2 client. L2 bodies come from the partitioned accessors, and receipts paired with them are filtered by type.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: op-core/fees: port the FastLZ and Fjord L1-cost cross-implementation fuzzers from op-e2e/opgeth
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20265 → #20257. Blocks #20275 (delete `op-e2e/opgeth`).

## Problem

[`op-e2e/opgeth/fastlz_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-e2e/opgeth/fastlz_test.go#L78-L231) holds the only checks of the Fjord fee math across implementations:

- [`FuzzFastLzGethSolidity`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-e2e/opgeth/fastlz_test.go#L194) compares Go FastLZ compressed length with Solidity `LibZip`, running a wrapper contract on a simulated backend.
- [`FuzzFastLzCgo`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-e2e/opgeth/fastlz_test.go#L231) compares Go FastLZ with the C reference in [`op-e2e/fastlz`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-e2e/fastlz).
- [`FuzzFjordCostFunction`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-e2e/opgeth/fastlz_test.go#L78) compares the Go Fjord L1 cost with `GasPriceOracle.getL1Fee`, run on an in-process op-geth L2.

They test op-geth's `types.FlzCompressLen` / `NewL1CostFunc` / `NewRollupCostData`. Deleting the package (#20275) would drop them.

They are behind the `cgo_test` build tag and run only from the `fuzz` target in [`op-e2e/justfile`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-e2e/justfile#L59-L60), which CI does not invoke.

## Work

- Move the three fuzzers next to [`op-core/fees`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/de9b6bb45823e4c45fc7d526e48c1e9d1e35bf45/op-core/fees), retargeted to `fees.FlzCompressLen`, `fees.NewRollupCostData` and `fees.L1CostFjord`.
  - The cgo and contract-backed parts need a home that may import `op-e2e/fastlz` and the `GasPriceOracle` bindings. A test-only package under `op-core/fees` or a surviving op-e2e package both work.
  - Keep the build tag if cgo stays required.
- `FuzzFjordCostFunction` currently calls the oracle on the package's in-process op-geth L2 (`op_geth.go`), which goes away with the package. Give it another backend: either an upstream simulated backend with the `GasPriceOracle`/`L1Block` predeploys and their fee storage set, or an op-reth L2.
- Read the fee parameters from the op-core/L1Block layout, not op-geth's `types.*Slot` constants.
- Optionally wire a short fuzz run into CI. It is cheap insurance for consensus-relevant math.

## Acceptance criteria

- The three fuzzers run against `op-core/fees`.
- Nothing in them imports an op-geth-only symbol.
- #20275 can delete `op-e2e/opgeth` without losing coverage.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: check below-head interop messages against log commitments
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Part 2 of 3. #23361 adds the log-commitment program, this PR checks messages against its proofs in the consolidation, and PR 3 makes the proposer request those proofs.

Today the SP1 consolidation loads every receipt of an initiating block to check one message. For a full 30M-gas block, that is about 72M PGU and 3.7 MB of witness per message, and any log in the expiry window is a valid target. This PR checks a message into a block below the initiating chain's local-safe head against the block's entry from the log-commitment program (#23361) and a Merkle opening. That costs about 0.1M PGU per message, plus an EIP-2935 step for far blocks.

Cannon keeps the receipts path. A block without an entry also keeps it, so the proposer works unchanged until PR 3 requests sub-proofs. The public values, the game, and the contracts do not change. The consolidation stdin gains item 2: deploy the host before or with the new ELF, because an old host with the new ELF halts.

Testing: every `graph.rs` case runs through both paths. The ELF matches native with and without entries. A CPU-proved batch proves a consolidation, and entries that differ from the batch proof do not prove. Replacement rounds are tested at the graph level only.

topPRs.title: ops: add an op-geth decoupling ratchet check
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Adds a required CI check, `opgeth-ratchet`, that stops a package from taking on op-geth-only APIs it doesn't already use. It type-checks the whole tree, tests included, against the upstream go-ethereum version op-geth is based on, using a temporary go.mod. The op-geth-only uses it finds are compared against `ops/scripts/opgeth-ratchet/allowlist.txt`:

- A use that isn't listed fails the PR. To add one, the PR has to list it with a reason, so the dependency is a deliberate review decision. The allowlist header points to the decoupling doc for ways around it.
- An entry that is no longer used also fails. `just opgeth-ratchet-update` removes it, so the list only shrinks unless someone adds to it on purpose.

This differs from #21748's original design, a scheduled upstream build compared against a failing-package baseline:

- **It gates PRs instead of reporting after merge.** An audit of the seeded allowlist found production code that took up op-geth APIs after their op-core replacements existed; the stacked follow-up PR fixes those.
- **It uses go/types instead of `go build`/`go vet`.** go/types type-checks every package from source, so each package reports only its own uses. `go build` stops at the first failing layer, which makes a failing-package set useless as a ratchet.

Some entries are upstream backports, not OP code: op-geth carries go-ethereum features from releases after its base version. They have their own reason in the allowlist and go away when op-geth's base moves.

CI caches the build under its own key. It also caches the few upstream modules the shared module cache lacks, so a module proxy outage doesn't fail the check.

Closes #21748

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: send L1 transactions with txmgr-style fee bumping
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
op-zk-proposer published each L1 transaction once, at the `pending` nonce, with no fee bumps and no RPC timeouts. One underpriced transaction queued every later transaction behind it. `resolve_in_flight_creation` then held proposals while `pending > latest`, so proposing stopped. A hung L1 or op-signer call blocked all sends, because the signer mutex was held across it. One receipt RPC error aborted the wait, and the next cycle sent a duplicate.

The proposer now sends the way Go `op-service/txmgr` does:
- It takes the `latest` nonce, so a send replaces a stuck transaction of ours.
- It bumps fees every 24s and when the pool says "underpriced".
- If a bump fails, it publishes the current version again.
- Each RPC and signer call times out after 10s, and the whole send is bounded by `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_TX_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT`.

`MAX_FEE_PER_GAS` and `MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_PER_GAS` now also cap fee bumps. There are no new config options.

**Compared with Go txmgr.** The nonce source, fee formula, +10% replacement bump, nonce-too-low abort rules and confirmation rule are the same. The differences:
- Two cases txmgr does not handle. A publish that gets no answer counts as published, and its hash is polled; txmgr drops it and can abort a send that actually landed. Receipts for all versions are queried at once, and the first confirmed one returns.
- Left out, because the proposer sends one transaction at a time: the fee-limit multiplier (bumps are bounded by the tick rate, the timeout and the fee caps), minimum tip and base-fee floors, gas re-estimation on bumps, rebroadcast, nonce-too-high retries, the mempool deadline, blobs, concurrent sends and metrics. The `tx_sender.rs` module doc lists them.

**Why not import base's `base-tx-manager`.**
- It cannot be a git dependency: `deny.toml`, rustc 1.96 and tokio 1.53 all block it. So we would own a copy of about 218 KB of source.
- Most of that code serves concurrent senders (a nonce reservation pool, `send_async`, a queue, blobs). The proposer uses none of it.
- It differs from txmgr exactly where this PR is needed. An "underpriced" first publish aborts the send, which is the restart wedge fixed here. A failed bump is never published again. The fee-limit check compares against the suggested fee instead of the bumped fee.
- Fixing those points means rewriting its send loop, so Base's production record would not carry over.

Tx metrics are planned as follow-up work for the op-proposer cutover. The ZK challenger already sends through Go txmgr (`op-challenger/game/zk`), so this PR covers the Rust side of the issue.

**Review finding deferred:** the scenario harness's `FakeActionExecutor` (`proposer/scenario/world.rs`) still models a mempool that queues later nonces. Production now replaces at the `latest` nonce. Production behaviour does not depend on this, but scenario tests with a timed-out transaction no longer match production. Updating the harness is separate work.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18428

topPRs.title: op-devstack: add a windowed proof oracle to the L2 EL DSL
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Why

Every proofs-store corruption so far (wipe handling, masked-trie overlays, the withdrawalsRoot bug, the crash gap) shows up as a wrong `eth_getProof` for some historical block. This adds one DSL sweep that catches all of them without knowing the cause, so the proofs-history scenario tests (#23380, #23383, #23389, #23390, #23395, #23396, #23398) can share a single oracle.

## What

**`op-devstack/dsl/l2_el_proofs.go`**

- `L2ELNode.VerifyHistoricalProofsMatch(reference, opts...)`: reads the node's proofs window from `debug_proofsSyncStatus`, waits (bounded) for the store to reach the sweep's last block, then for every sampled block fetches `eth_getProof` by block hash for `L2ToL1MessagePasser` plus the configured accounts from the node under test and from `reference`, Merkle-verifies both against the header's state root, requires them equal after normalization, and requires the message passer's storage root to equal the header's `withdrawalsRoot` (post-Isthmus, i.e. whenever the header value is not the empty withdrawals hash). Headers are fetched from both nodes and must agree on the hash. The window is re-read at every block: a block the pruner removes during the sweep is skipped when the caller did not pin `FirstBlock`, and fails the sweep otherwise. The reference must answer `debug_proofsSyncStatus` with method-not-found, which only a node without a proofs-history store does.
- `HistoricalProofsOpts`: `Accounts []ProofAccount` (address + storage keys), `CatchUpTimeout` (default 30s), `FirstBlock`/`LastBlock` (zero = window edge at sweep start), `MaxSampledBlocks` (zero = every block; edges always included).
- `VerifyProofsMatchAt(reference, block, accounts...)`: single-block form (listed accounts only, no independence check); `ProofsSyncStatus()` and `WaitForProofsStoreBlock(target, timeout)` expose the sync status RPC.
- `NormalizeProofResponse` and `VerifyAccountProof` moved here from `rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/utils/proof.go`. The normalizer additionally turns an empty storage proof list into nil so geth and reth responses compare equal; the verifier additionally rejects a nonzero storage value claimed under an empty storage root. `utils/proof.go` and `utils.WaitForProofsStoreBlock` are deleted; `proofs/core`, `proofs/prune` and `proofs/reorg` call the DSL methods instead and drop the waits `VerifyProofsMatchAt` performs itself.

**`op-devstack/sysgo`**

- `OpRethConfig.ProofsHistoryWindow` + `OpRethWithProofsHistoryWindow(blocks)`: the runtime passes `--proofs-history.window` itself and op-reth rejects a repeated flag, so the window is a config field (`proofsHistoryNodeArgs` emits it once; default stays 10000). #23389 and #23390 reuse it.
- `OpRethWithEthProofWindow(blocks)`: reth's `--rpc.eth-proof-window` defaults to 0, so a node without proofs history rejects every historical `eth_getProof` with `ExceedsMaxProofWindow`. A reference node needs this.

**`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_match`**

`TestProofsHistoryFollowerServesMatchingHistoricalProofs`: a sequencer started with `OpRethWithoutProofsHistory()` + `OpRethWithEthProofWindow` is the independent reference; a follower runs proofs history under the matrix cell's flags. Four rounds of: two EOAs transfer back and forth, one initiates a withdrawal (so the message passer's storage root changes inside the swept range), and one calls a contract that SSTOREs `NUMBER` and `TIMESTAMP`. Before the last round the test waits for the follower to pass `persistence-threshold + 2 * memory-block-buffer-target` blocks, so reth has persisted at least once and the sweep spans blocks on both sides of that. The follower is then swept from the window's first block to the last workload block for the message passer, both EOAs and the contract's two slots.

Matrix (table-driven subtests): persistence threshold {7, 50} x state masking {0, 30} x proofs path {index = `verification-interval=0`, execute = `verification-interval=1`}. The four `masking_30` cells skip naming ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#457 (the flag does not exist on develop's reth 2.5.2 build and #23046 rejects a nonzero value).

Unit tests: `VerifyAccountProof` against a synthetic state trie (valid account with storage, without storage, absent account, zero slot under an empty root; tampered balance, tampered storage value, nonzero slot under an empty root, absent account claiming a balance, wrong root), `NormalizeProofResponse` (five cases), `ProofsSyncStatus.serves` (five), `sampleBlockNumbers` (seven), `proofsHistoryNodeArgs` and the two new options.

## Local verification

```
go test -count=1 ./op-devstack/dsl/ -run 'TestVerifyAccountProof|TestNormalizeProofResponse|TestSampleBlockNumbers|TestProofsSyncStatusServes'   # ok
go test -count=1 ./op-devstack/sysgo/ -run 'TestProofsHistoryNodeArgs|TestOpRethWith'                                                         # ok

DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=.../target/debug/op-reth \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -v -run TestProofsHistoryFollowerServesMatchingHistoricalProofs \
  ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_match/
--- PASS: threshold_7-masking_0-index (58.61s)      sweep: 26 blocks x 4 accounts
--- PASS: threshold_7-masking_0-execute (56.88s)    sweep: 25 blocks x 4 accounts
--- PASS: threshold_50-masking_0-index (136.96s)    sweep: 66 blocks x 4 accounts
--- PASS: threshold_50-masking_0-execute (154.70s)  sweep: 65 blocks x 4 accounts
--- SKIP: threshold_{7,50}-masking_30-{index,execute}   (protocol-team#457)
```

An earlier run without `LastBlock` pinned showed the catch-up wait firing (`Proofs store behind target ... window [0, 20]`) while the sweep's last block was still buffered in the ExEx.

Proofs e2e suite after the migration (`rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/core`, both nodes op-reth, debug binary):

```
--- PASS: TestL2MultipleTransactionsInDifferentBlocks (37.23s)
--- PASS: TestL2MultipleTransactionsInSingleBlock (27.24s)
--- PASS: TestExecutePayloadSuccess (17.41s)
--- PASS: TestExecutePayloadWithInvalidParentHash (17.63s)
--- PASS: TestDebugExecutionWitness (26.82s)
--- PASS: TestResyncing (43.42s)
--- PASS: TestStorageProofUsingSimpleStorageContract (46.79s)
--- PASS: TestStorageProofUsingMultiStorageContract (67.78s)
--- PASS: TestTokenVaultStorageProofs (37.37s)
ok  	github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/core	322.780s
EXIT=0

```

Not run: the kona-node CL variant (`DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`; no kona-node binary built locally). The `prune` and `reorg` packages compile but stay dormant as before.

### Corruption check (not committed)

A copy of the test started the follower with `sysgo.OpRethWithProofsHistoryWindow(20)`, ran three times the workload so the pruner moved `earliest` to 25, and swept with `opts.FirstBlock = 1`:

```
Sweeping historical proofs  name=proofs-follower reference=sequencer window="[25, 45]" first=1 last=45 blocks=45 accounts=4
Error:      Should be true
Messages:   proofs store on proofs-follower does not serve block 1: window [25, 45]
--- FAIL: TestCorruptionCheckSmallerWindowBites (101.42s)
```

The sweep fails before any account is fetched, because the store no longer serves the block at all; a wrong proof for a served block fails one level deeper with `block N account 0x..: eth_getProof from <node> does not verify against state root ...` / `... differs from reference <node>`, which the unit tests exercise with tampered proofs.

## Findings

- op-reth's `eth_getProof` rejects a `null` storage-key list (`Invalid params: invalid type: null, expected a sequence`) where op-geth accepts it. The old helpers always passed `[]common.Hash{}`; the DSL now sends an empty list for a nil `StorageKeys`.
- While that bug made every `eth_getProof` fail fast, three of four cells ended their 30s retry window with `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>: i/o timeout` against the follower's user-RPC proxy, the symptom `safeheaddb_elsync` already skips on op-reth. It did not recur once requests stopped failing; noted in case it shows up again.
- Deviation from the issue text: the issue assumes the devstack sequencer always runs proofs history and asks for a separate reference node. The test instead turns proofs history off on the sequencer (`MixedSingleChainNodeSpec.OpRethOpts`), which is the production shape and saves a third node. The verification criterion expects the smaller-window failure to name "the block and account"; the oracle fails earlier, at the window check, naming the block, the node and the window (see above).

## Seams for the sibling PRs

- `L2ELNode.VerifyHistoricalProofsMatch` / `VerifyProofsMatchAt` / `WaitForProofsStoreBlock` / `ProofsSyncStatus`.
- `sysgo.OpRethWithProofsHistoryWindow`, `sysgo.OpRethWithEthProofWindow` (a reference node needs the latter together with `OpRethWithoutProofsHistory`).

Closes #23379

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: cover proofs re-execution across a sequencer reorg
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Why

The proofs-history ExEx handles a reth reorg notification by unwinding its store to the fork point and indexing the replacement blocks from reth's trie data; a follower on the re-execution path (`--proofs-history.verification-interval=1`) then executes every block that follows against the unwound state, including calls into code that only a replacement block created. The only coverage was an ExEx unit test with a hand-built replacement block; the real notification sequence of a sequencer reorg, with a fork point in reth's memory or below its persisted tip, had never been run against the proof oracle. #23046 changes what happens when a replaced block fails re-execution, so this is the acceptance coverage for it.

## What

**`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg`** (sequencer without proofs history as the `eth_getProof` reference and the node the test sequencer drives, follower re-executing every block, 1s L2 blocks, both op-reths with `--engine.persistence-threshold` and `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target=5` passed explicitly):

- `TestProofsHistoryFollowerMatchesTheReplacementChainAfterASequencerReorg`: the batcher is stopped up front so the replaced blocks never reach L1; four EOAs are funded, traffic runs past the setup and op-node's sequencer stops, which makes its head the fork point; an in-memory cell then pads the chain with empty test-sequencer blocks until the replaced blocks will leave the fork point in reth's memory by the persistence model, so the fork point does not depend on where the stop landed. The test sequencer then builds the `depth` blocks the reorg will replace on top of it, no faster than wall-clock (op-node rejects a gossiped payload more than 5s ahead), and the follower imports them by gossip and re-executes them; the test waits until its proofs store has flushed the last of them. The test sequencer then builds one conflicting block on the fork point, the batcher restarts and op-node resumes sequencing on top of it. The follower must adopt the replacement chain (`ReorgExact` on the first replaced height), survive (no `panicked` line), catch up, serve the replacement block with its transactions, and after ten more blocks of traffic `VerifyHistoricalProofsMatch` sweeps every block from the fork point to the last traffic block for the four EOAs and, in the deployed-contract workload, the recorder's two slots; that workload also requires the recorder's slot 0 on the follower to hold a block number above the fork point. Finally the follower's op-reth log must show the ExEx reorg notification and the proofs engine unwinding stored blocks, and must show reth's "on-disk reorg detected" line exactly in the on-disk cells.
- Workloads: `deployed_contract` (the first replaced block deploys the `NUMBER`/`TIMESTAMP` recorder and the replaced blocks after it call it; the replacement block carries the same deployment transaction, so the contract exists at the same address, plus a call into it; the traffic after the reorg keeps calling it) and `plain_transfers`.
- Depths per threshold: 2 (fork point among the blocks reth never persisted), 6 (deeper than the memory block buffer target, fork point still in memory; at threshold 7 reth holds 5 to 7 blocks, so up to two padding blocks are needed), and 12 at threshold 7 / 55 at threshold 50 (below reth's persisted tip: on-disk reorg). `blocksInRethMemory` models reth's persistence schedule and `matrix_test.go` pins it; the assertion on reth's own "on-disk reorg detected" line, present in exactly the on-disk cells, catches a wrong model instead of silently testing the other path. Note the issue's "threshold + 5" bound for the on-disk depth is conservative: reth holds at most `threshold` blocks (it persists once the head is more than the threshold above the persisted tip, down to the head minus the buffer target).

Matrix, as table-driven subtests: threshold {7, 50} x masking {0, 30} x workload {deployed_contract, plain_transfers} x depth {in memory shallow, in memory deep, on disk}. The masking cells skip naming ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#457. Under `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node` every cell skips: the test sequencer commits and publishes blocks through op-node's `opstack_commitBlockV1`/`opstack_publishBlockV1` RPCs, which kona-node does not serve.

**`op-devstack`** seams:

- Log recorder: `logpipe.LogRecord` (entries whose message, or raw text for a line that is not structured JSON such as a panic hook's output, contains a substring) and `logpipe.LogRecords` (fan-out), `stack.LogRecorder`, `sysgo.OpReth.RecordLogLines(substring)` recording every stdout and stderr line at every level across restarts, forwarded by the preset `l2ELFrontend`, and `dsl.L2ELNode.RecordLogLines(substring)`, which fails for a node whose log the devstack does not expose. `logpipe.StructuredRustLogEntry.UnparsedLine()` exposes the raw text of an unstructured line.
- `dsl.EOA.PlanBlockRecorderDeployment()`: the recorder deployment as a planned transaction, so a test can keep its signed bytes; `DeployBlockRecorder` uses it.
- `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlockWithTxs` closes out the job with `Next` after a successful publish (every step is already done, so `Next` only resets), which lets consecutive blocks be sequenced on one chain; before, the second `New` failed with `block already sealed`. No existing caller sequenced two blocks on the same chain. A block that was not published still leaves the job sealed, as before, now with a warning.
- `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlockWithTxsWhenDue(t, network, parent, rawTxs)`: builds the block no earlier than its timestamp (fixed by its height) so op-node's gossip validation accepts it on publish and on receipt. The wait is a wall-clock wait inside the DSL, since the chain stands still while the test sequencer drives it.

Deleted `rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/reorg/reorg_test.go`: dormant (CI runs `proofs/core` only), it used sleeps and tested the index path; its reorg coverage is superseded here. Unit tests: `TestLogRecordKeepsMatchingEntriesInOrder`, `TestLogRecordMatchesTheRawTextOfUnstructuredLines`, `TestLogRecordEntriesIsACopy`, `TestLogRecordsFanOutFromRegistration`, `TestBlocksInRethMemory`, `TestInMemoryDepthsFitRethMemoryWithinOnePersistenceCycle`, `TestOnDiskDepthsExceedRethMemory`.

## Findings

- How a CL-synced follower adopts an unsafe reorg: op-node drops every gossiped block that does not extend its unsafe chain (`skipping unsafe payload, since it is older than unsafe head` / `does not build onto the existing unsafe chain`), so the replacement blocks below its head never get in through gossip. Once a gossiped block above its head arrives, `checkForGapInUnsafeQueue` hands it to reth with `engine_newPayload`; reth fetches the missing replacement blocks from its EL peer (`Block added to fork chain`) and makes the forkchoice target canonical once they connect. The follower switched 2s after op-node resumed in the in-memory cells and 4s in the on-disk ones; L1 derivation was not involved. The batcher still has to be off while the replaced blocks are built, or they become safe and the fork is impossible.
- The bump's `Block left reth's chain during proofs execution` line (and develop's `Parent state not available in reth; skipping execute_block` skip) only fires when the ExEx is mid-execution of a block of the old chain at the instant reth reorgs. With a real reorg the ExEx has long finished the old chain by then (it executes a block in about a millisecond), so neither line appeared in any cell (`parent_state_missing_skips=0 left_chain_handoffs=0`), and neither can be asserted deterministically without a seam that delays ExEx execution. The test records both counts and logs them; the issue's expectation that a deeper reorg makes the line appear does not hold.
- The reorg notification carries the whole replacement chain in one go: `reorg_depth=4 common_ancestor=20` for a depth-2 reorg, since reth connects the fetched blocks and the block that followed before it switches.
- On develop every cell matches the oracle, including the on-disk reorgs at both thresholds (reth rebuilds the replaced persisted blocks with overlay-computed trie updates for the notification, and the ExEx's fork-block check holds).
